newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest office space being locked in - Collier's.
newsitem.headline: Budapest office space being locked in - Collier's.

text.p: Large corporations moving operations to Budapest are locking up deals on large amounts of the Hungarian capital's prime office space, Colliers International said.

"One of the factors which affected the market at the end of 1996, and which can be expected to continue, is the selection of Budapest as the location for the central and eastern European headquarters of an increasing number of firms," Colliers said in a research report.

"During 1996 Shell, Lucent Technologies and Opel decided to locate their Central and Eastern European operations in Budapest, while Pepsi moved their European headquarters to the city," the real estate services company said.
It said it had found an increasing number of large firms willing to make deals for five- or 10-year leases on projects still under construction or in the planning stages.
"Thus while the vacancy rate in the Budapest office market today is high, for many larger tenants the options are limited and landlords can exercise significant power in negotiations," Colliers said.

"Colliers does not believe that this situation will change significantly over the next several years, as absorption and new supply are expected to be almost euqal during 1998 at some 47,000 square metres."
